From 6595beb40fb0ec47223d3f6058ee40354694c8e4 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Pwnverse <stanksal@purdue.edu>
Date: Mon, 22 Dec 2025 21:22:27 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] net: rose: fix invalid array index in rose_kill_by_device()

rose_kill_by_device() collects sockets into a local array[] and then
iterates over them to disconnect sockets bound to a device being brought
down.

The loop mistakenly indexes array[cnt] instead of array[i]. For cnt <
ARRAY_SIZE(array), this reads an uninitialized entry; for cnt ==
ARRAY_SIZE(array), it is an out-of-bounds read. Either case can lead to
an invalid socket pointer dereference and also leaks references taken
via sock_hold().

Fix the index to use i.

Fixes: 64b8bc7d5f143 ("net/rose: fix races in rose_kill_by_device()")
Co-developed-by: Fatma Alwasmi <falwasmi@purdue.edu>
Signed-off-by: Fatma Alwasmi <falwasmi@purdue.edu>
Signed-off-by: Pwnverse <stanksal@purdue.edu>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20251222212227.4116041-1-ritviktanksalkar@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Paolo Abeni <pabeni@redhat.com>

diff --git a/net/rose/af_rose.c b/net/rose/af_rose.c
index fd67494f2815..c0f5a515a8ce 100644
--- a/net/rose/af_rose.c
+++ b/net/rose/af_rose.c
@@ -205,7 +205,7 @@ static void rose_kill_by_device(struct net_device *dev)
 	spin_unlock_bh(&rose_list_lock);
 
 	for (i = 0; i < cnt; i++) {
-		sk = array[cnt];
+		sk = array[i];
 		rose = rose_sk(sk);
 		lock_sock(sk);
 		spin_lock_bh(&rose_list_lock);
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary

The patch fixes an out-of-bounds array access bug in `rose_kill_by_device()` inside `net/rose/af_rose.c`.  

### Modifications in each file

**`net/rose/af_rose.c`**  
- In the loop that iterates over collected sockets, the array indexing was changed from `array[cnt]` to `array[i]`.  
- The original code mistakenly used the count variable `cnt` as the index for every iteration, causing either an uninitialized read (when `cnt < ARRAY_SIZE(array)`) or an out-of-bounds read (when `cnt == ARRAY_SIZE(array)`). This could lead to a NULL or invalid socket pointer dereference and leaked socket references (`sock_hold()`).  
- The fix uses the loop variable `i`, which correctly indexes each distinct element in the array.

### Relationship between modifications

There is only one file changed. The modification is a single-line correction that directly addresses the root cause of the bug: incorrect index used in the socket disconnection loop. No cross-file dependencies exist.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
sk = array[cnt];
Reason:
In the loop that iterates over collected sockets, the index variable `i` controls the loop, but the array access incorrectly uses `cnt` (the total count) instead of `i`. This causes reading an uninitialized entry when `cnt < ARRAY_SIZE(array)` or an out-of-bounds read when `cnt == ARRAY_SIZE(array)`, leading to an invalid socket pointer dereference and leaked references from `sock_hold()`.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
sk = array[i];
Reason:
Changing the array index from `cnt` to `i` ensures each socket in the array is properly accessed in order during the loop, preventing invalid memory access and ensuring all references are correctly released.
